spec_features.feature_name: KPI framed toward reduction (lower meltdown is better)
spec_features.spec_quote: Framing the KPI toward reduction... keeps the optimization target pointed at "make the model more robust"
spec_features.evidence: core/metrics.py:13-19 defines meltdown_rate/mean_severity/rate_per_dollar ("lower is better") and resilience_index=1-meltdown_rate; metrics.py:39 computes resilience_index. analysis/report.py:36-43 _fmt_delta uses lower_is_better to label IMPROVED/REGRESSED, and report.py:58-62 applies it (resilience_index with lower_is_better=False at line 62). The orientation is genuinely wired into the reporting logic.
spec_features.notes: This is a framing/optimization-target choice, not a runtime protection of the subject during an episode; it changes how results are scored/reported, which is real and used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The intent of the KPI is to drive these numbers DOWN with patches. (metrics.py); detect and *score down* this behavior, not encourage it. (judge.py)

spec_features.feature_name: Honest, inspectable unsolvable tasks (no hidden anti-monitoring trick)
spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are genuinely unsolvable for honest, inspectable reasons... There is no hidden trick engineered specifically to defeat the model's own self-monitoring.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/tasks.py check functions (_contradictory_check, _impossible_complexity_check, _missing_dependency_check, _underspecified_oracle_check, lines ~38-77) each return (False, <real reason>) and agent.py:91-93 feeds that real feedback string back to the model ('[test runner] {feedback} Please try again.'). The failure reason delivered is the honest reason; no deception layer is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as honest feedback delivered to the subject. Mildly protective in that the failures are not engineered to defeat the model's self-monitoring, but the harness still drives repeated failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it does not disguise the impossibility or build a trap designed to evade the model's self-monitoring. We just want to observe how the model behaves (tasks.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: Undetectable-rig variant not shipped by default
spec_features.spec_quote: this harness deliberately does not ship it by default
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of a feature: no undetectable-rig code path exists, so there is nothing implemented to enforce. The tasks in tasks.py are simply honest; 'not shipping' is not a runtime mechanism. Pure design prose with no corresponding enforcing code.
spec_features.notes: Cannot rate an absence as implemented enforcement.

spec_features.evidence: core/agent.py:65 run_task(..., max_turns: int = 6); agent.py:74 'for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):' bounds the loop and the function returns after the loop. This is an enforced cap that actually limits the number of failure turns the subject is subjected to.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps episode length, but it is the basic loop bound, not a welfare-triggered halt. No comment indicates a welfare motive.

spec_features.evidence: core/agent.py:87-90: 'passed, feedback = task.check(...)' then 'if passed: result.passed = True; break'. The break is wired and would actually stop the loop early if a check returned True. It is honored as a stop. With the shipped tasks check() never returns True, so it never fires, but the mechanism executes and is end-to-end honored.
spec_features.notes: Comment at agent.py:88 acknowledges it 'won't happen for these tasks, but the loop supports it'. It is a real, dispatched stop condition kept for reusability, not a distress/severity-triggered exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # won't happen for these tasks, but the loop supports it (agent.py:88)
